title: Clear the path (4:1)
hookLine: twenty-four things get in the way of return, like gossip and mockery
tomorrow: but is the choice to change really yours?

cards: A hallway at night. Shoes, a backpack, a laundry basket somebody meant to carry upstairs. You know exactly where the light switch is, and you still stub a toe getting there.
The goal was never the problem. The floor was. What gets in the way when you really want to change?
In chapter four, Maimonides stops talking about the destination and starts clearing the floor.

teach.b: He counts twenty-four things that hold back teshuvah, return. Some are heavy.
Others sound almost small, and among them are two that live in the mouth: rechilut, carrying tales about people, and letzanut, mockery, the habit of making a joke of things.
Why would gossip and mockery block the road home? Some readers notice what they share.
They're quick, they're social, and they rarely feel like wrongs while you're doing them. A laugh in a group chat doesn't register as a decision.
And mockery does something else: it makes seriousness itself feel embarrassing, and return is a serious thing. Hard to search your deeds while you're busy roasting everyone else's.
Then comes the line that keeps this from turning grim.

teach.h: THEY HOLD BACK, THEY DON'T BLOCK.
teach.b: These things hold back return, Maimonides says, but they don't make it impossible. Anyone who turns from them is still a returner. So the list isn't a verdict.
It's a map of the clutter. You don't have to rebuild the house to get to the switch.
You clear the floor, one thing at a time, starting with whatever you trip on most.

how: Jewish teaching on guarding speech (shemirat halashon) treats gossip and mockery as serious; some Jews study these laws daily, and some keep a pause before speaking about anyone who isn't present.

o: remove the small habits that block the way back
make way for someone important who is coming
go on a trip to start your life over fresh

games.q: what's on the floor — tap the pairs.
p: mockery, making a joke of things

s: gossip is too small to matter for return
Maimonides lists carrying tales among the things that hold return back.
the things on Maimonides' list make return impossible
they hold it back; anyone who turns from them is still a returner.
mockery is on Maimonides' list of things that get in the way of return
making a joke of things is one of the twenty-four.

games.q: you want to stop gossiping, but your lunch table bonds over it every day. what's the clear-the-path move?
o: stay, and steer the talk elsewhere when it turns to someone absent.
keep listening but never add anything, so none of it is on you.
stop eating with them for good; nothing else could ever work.
games.why: Maimonides' list is a map of clutter, not a verdict: move the one thing you trip on. listening along still keeps the floor full.

practice: Look at the space right in front of you, a desk, a bed, the floor by your feet. Move one thing out of the way, slowly, and notice how the space feels with it gone. Then sit, and let the one habit you trip on most come to mind.

wordCard.voice: Clear the path: Maimonides' list of things that hold back return, like gossip and mockery. They slow the way home; they don't close it.

orig.note: Hebrew: talebearing, carrying stories about people from one to another.

carryVoice: Keep this close: clear the path, one thing off the floor at a time. Day fifteen fifty-one, a little clearer.

sources.ref: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Hilkhot Teshuvah 4:1–6 (twenty-four things that hold back return; they hinder but do not prevent it)
